newsitem.title: UK: US stocks hold firm in London, IBM extends gains.
newsitem.headline: US stocks hold firm in London, IBM extends gains.

text.p: Most U.S. stocks were firmer in London on Tuesday, led by shares in International Business Machines Corp (IBM), which got a boost from a buy recommendation from Goldman Sachs, dealers said.
London dealers said they were expecting Wall Street to open higher as long as the retail sales figures for April, due at 1230 GMT, were not too far out of line with market expectations.
Economists surveyed by Reuters were expecting sales to show a 0.3 percent drop.
"The market is trading better and we're still seeing interest in the technology stocks, especially IBM," a London dealer said.
Goldman initiated coverage of the computer giant, placing it on the firm's recommended list, dealers said. The only higher buy rating is Goldman's priority list.
IBM shares were quoted as high as $174 in London, up $2-1/8, after jumping $4-3/8 in New York on Monday.
Intel Corp shares were up $1/4 to $159-3/8. Most other technology shares were up $1/8 to $1/4, but shares in Apple Computer Inc slipped $1/4, dealers said.
In other trading, shares in Philip Morris Co Inc added $1/4 in London to $42-3/4.
June S&P 500 futures were down 0.05 points to 841.30 at 1027 GMT. June long bond futures were down 1/32 at 110-11/32.

"Futures haven't been a great indication of the market lately," another dealer said. "But (the market) looks set to go higher. For the most part, earnings have been strong and the bond market has been supportive."
